summary: Reject action deletes shared EXPRESSES edge, orphaning accepted sibling tags

analysis.content: Discovered while auditing 53a46a8d (concept ID format mismatch). The premise of 53a46a8d was incorrect — bare IDs in staged_tags are BY DESIGN (apply-time prefixing per docs/concept-hierarchy/design.md:32 and confirmed by scripts/review_tags.py:90-123, guru-review/server/src/apply.ts:82-94). Live DB verification: 30,294 of 30,349 accepted tags have matching EXPRESSES edges (99.9% coverage).
analysis.author: corpus-quality

analysis.content: 55 accepted tags are missing their EXPRESSES edges. ALL 55 have a rejected sibling for the same (chunk_id, concept_id) pair from a different model. The reject action deletes the shared edge unconditionally, even when an accepted sibling tag still supports it.
analysis.author: corpus-quality

analysis.content: All 55 are in christian_mysticism (49) and buddhism (6). All have siblings of the form [(accepted, 1), (rejected, 1)] across models Qwen3.5-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf and qwen-3-4b-guru-v3-Q4_K_M.ggfu / Carnice-9b.
analysis.author: corpus-quality

analysis.content: This is an apply-path defect in the review app's reject logic: when a tag is rejected, the apply script deletes the EXPRESSES edge without checking whether other accepted tags still reference the same (chunk, concept) pair. Fix: check for surviving accepted tags before deleting the edge.
analysis.author: corpus-quality
corpus-quality
analysis.content: FIXED BY CORPUS-QUALITY: Ran scripts/restore_missing_edges.py --apply after DB backup (corpus-quality-d9bb3b9a). Restored 55 EXPRESSES edges at tier=verified. Verified: 0 missing edges remain, 0 duplicates created. Manifest diff: edges +55, all other tables unchanged.

resolution.note: Both apply paths (review_tags.py reject_tag, web apply.ts) now check for a surviving accepted sibling before deleting the shared EXPRESSES edge. Data repair of the 55 orphaned edges was already applied by corpus-quality (restore_missing_edges.py, backup corpus-quality-d9bb3b9a).
